statement_utf8: Erdős: Is there a prime between n^(2)and (n+1)^(2 )for every n > 0?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For every positive integer n, find a prime strictly between consecutive squares. A finite primality sweep cannot control all intervals; Bertrand's factor-two interval is too long. No uniform short-interval mechanism established.
source_name_literal: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős)

statement_utf8: /Riasanovsky: Let f be the formal power series over Z/2Z whose nth coefficient is the parity of the divisor function Ă_(0)(n). Is it true that the density of 1's in the power series 1/f is 1/32?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Quantifier is limiting natural density of reciprocal-series coefficients over F2. Divisor notation is corrupted and f(0) is unspecified; invertibility requires constant coefficient 1. Do not silently supply it or infer density from a prefix.
source_name_literal: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Riasanovsky)

statement_utf8: Let subharmonic functions $u_k$ on the unit square converge uniformly to $u(x,y)=x$. If $D_k=\{u_k<0\}$ and $D_k^*$ is the component containing $-1/2$, can $D_k\setminus D_k^*$ meet every horizontal segment $[-1+it,1+it]$, $-1<t<1$?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Uniformly convergent sequence of subharmonic functions; ask whether other negative components hit every horizontal line. Unit-square convention conflicts with displayed [-1,1] coordinates, and eventual/all-k quantifier needs source. Uniform convergence confines extra components near x=0 but does not forbid thin channels.
source_name_literal: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

statement_utf8: Let $f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb P^2$ be linearly nondegenerate and let $\delta(a,f)$ be the Nevanlinna deficiency of a point $a\in\mathbb P^2$. Prove that for every system of points in general position, $$\sum_a\delta(a,f)\le1.$$
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For every linearly nondegenerate entire curve and general-position point system, total point defect at most one. Point defect needs exact counting convention. Hyperplane second-main-theorem bounds do not directly give this codimension-two constant; no local certificate.
source_name_literal: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

statement_utf8: For every positive integer $k$, let $R_k$ be a $1/k$ by $1/(k+1)$ rectangle. Can the entire collection $(R_k)_{k\ge1}$ be packed without overlap into the unit square?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All reciprocal rectangles simultaneously in one square; finite packings or total area one do not give compatible infinite placements. Tail area 1/(N+1) is necessary bookkeeping only. No full-scope constructive placement found.
source_name_literal: Eppstein - The Geometry Junkyard: Open Problems (proposed by David Eppstein and cited proposers)

statement_utf8: For Ollivier's coarse Ricci curvature, smooth uniformly strictly log-concave measures on $\mathbb{R}^N$ have positive curvature. What can be said for a general log-concave measure? In particular, analyze a convex body equipped with Brownian motion conditioned not to leave it.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: General log-concave probability measures and conditioned Brownian motion on convex bodies. Curvature depends on the transition kernel, time and metric; nonnegative Hessian coupling alone does not answer all conditioned-process cases. Open-ended request lacks one exact endpoint.
source_name_literal: Ollivier - Discrete Ricci curvature: Open problems (2008) (proposed by Yann Ollivier)

statement_utf8: Suppose the global infimum of coarse Ricci curvature is zero, while its infimum on every finite-radius ball about an origin is positive. Is there a systematic relation between the rate at which curvature tends to zero at infinity and the isoperimetric profile? Analyze, for example, the $M/M/k$ queue.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All spaces with locally positive coarse curvature and global infimum zero; asks systematic relation to isoperimetry, plus M/M/k example. Metric/kernel/rate normalization and target bound absent. Queue instance cannot settle a universal characterization.
source_name_literal: Ollivier - Discrete Ricci curvature: Open problems (2008) (proposed by Yann Ollivier)

statement_utf8: Are there geodesic flows or Birkhoff billiards with fractal caustics? More specifically, for every $1\leq s<2$, is there a caustic of a convex billiard with Hausdorff dimension $s$; and for every $s\geq1$, is there a Riemannian manifold $M$ and a point whose caustic has Hausdorff dimension $s$?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every real dimension s in [1,2) for convex-billiard caustics and every s>=1 for Riemannian point caustics. A fractal invariant set is not automatically a caustic with requested regularity. No construction meeting both universal clauses.
source_name_literal: Knill - Open problems in Hamiltonian dynamics (2000) (proposed by Oliver Knill)

statement_utf8: (a) Is the set of $n$-periodic orbits of a smooth strictly convex Birkhoff billiard nowhere dense for every $n$? (b) Does every polygonal Birkhoff billiard have a periodic orbit?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Two separate all-period/all-polygon assertions. Rational-angle polygon unfolding only treats a subclass; finite-period checks cannot prove nowhere density for every n. No full-scope route to both clauses.
source_name_literal: Knill - Open problems in Hamiltonian dynamics (2000)

statement_utf8: Let $A,B$ be irreducible integer matrices of the same spectral radius. Suppose $\operatorname{tr}(A^n)>0$ implies $\operatorname{tr}(B^n)>0$ for every $n$, and the dimension module of $B$ is a quotient of a closed submodule of that of $A$. Prove that the shift $S_B$ is a factor of $S_A$.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All admissible matrix pairs with common spectral radius and ordered dimension-module subquotient condition. Nonnegative adjacency convention and closed ordered submodule must be recovered; trace support is weaker than a factor construction. No bounded matrix test settles arbitrary sizes.
source_name_literal: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

statement_utf8: If $S$ and $T$ are mixing shifts of finite type, prove that $S^i$ and $T^j$ can commute for all sufficiently large integers $i,j$.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For every pair of mixing SFTs, all sufficiently large i,j should admit commuting realizations. Common underlying space and allowed conjugacies must be fixed. Comparing powers numerically cannot construct commuting actions.
source_name_literal: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

statement_utf8: For the symbolic system $X$ constructed in Section 14 of the source from a commuting pair of full-shift endomorphisms, is Haar measure its only invariant ergodic Borel probability measure with full support?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Uniqueness among full-support invariant ergodic probability measures for the Section14 symbolic system, not arbitrary shifts. X and the full acting group are absent; Bernoulli measures on a guessed shift would be an invalid counterexample.
source_name_literal: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

statement_utf8: With $\nu(f,S_N)$ defined as in Question 25.3, must every surjective one-dimensional cellular automaton satisfy $\nu(f,S_N)\ge\sqrt N$?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All surjective one-dimensional CA, with nu defined only through Question25.3, should satisfy nu>=sqrt(N). Missing definition of nu precludes a literal finite test. Surjectivity alone supplies no claimed periodic-point exponential bound.
source_name_literal: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

statement_utf8: Characterize the countable groups $G$ for which every injective $G$-equivariant cellular automaton on $A^G$, for every finite alphabet $A$, is surjective.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Characterize countable G satisfying injective-implies-surjective for every finite alphabet and equivariant CA. Finite or residually finite cases cannot characterize arbitrary groups. No obstruction or full classification mechanism.
source_name_literal: Boyle - Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (2008)

statement_utf8: Let $F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be smooth, have a fixed point, and satisfy $$\rho\bigl(|DF(x)|\bigr)<1\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^2.$$ Is the fixed point globally asymptotically stable?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every smooth planar F with a fixed point and rho(|DF(x)|)<1 everywhere should be globally asymptotically stable. Absolute-value matrix convention matters. Pointwise contractivity in varying weighted norms does not supply one uniform global contraction; no rigorous escaping orbit constructed.
source_name_literal: Gasull - Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems (2020) (proposed by Armengol Gasull)

statement_utf8: For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Pi(n)$ be the product of its decimal digits, and let $\operatorname{Pm}(n)$ be the least positive integer such that $\Pi^{\operatorname{Pm}(n)}(n)=\Pi^{\operatorname{Pm}(n)+1}(n)$. Is $\operatorname{Pm}(n)\leq11$ for every $n$?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All decimal integers should have multiplicative persistence <=11 under least-positive stabilization convention. Removing 0 and 1 digits reduces search but leaves unbounded prime-exponent triples. No finite bound reduction; no sweep attempted.
source_name_literal: Gasull - Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems (2020) (proposed by Armengol Gasull)

statement_utf8: Define $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ by $f(n)=n+\operatorname{rev}(n)$, where $\operatorname{rev}$ reverses the decimal digits. Are there infinitely many $n$ for which no iterate $f^k(n)$, $k>0$, is a palindrome? Is the least such $n$ equal to $196$?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Infinitely many non-palindrome-reaching reverse-add starts and minimal such start 196. Long finite trajectories cannot certify nontermination; terminal palindrome search below 196 cannot establish the infinite-orbit clause.
source_name_literal: Gasull - Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems (2020) (proposed by Armengol Gasull)

statement_utf8: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T_1,\ldots, T_\ell)$ be a system and $\{p_1,\ldots, p_\ell\}$ be a family of intersective integer polynomials. Show that for every set $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$ one has $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap \cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A)>0 $$ for some $n\in\mathbb N$.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For every positive-measure A and intersective polynomial family, some positive n gives simultaneous recurrence. Commutation and jointly-versus-separately intersective conventions are essential. Finite cyclic obstructions with incompatible roots would test a weaker misreading, not the source assertion.
source_name_literal: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

statement_utf8: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a probability space, $T_1,\ldots, T_\ell \colon X\to X$ be invertible measure preserving transformations, and $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Show that for every $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$ we have $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{m+p_1(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{m+p_\ell(n)}A)>0 $$ for some $m,n\in \mathbb N$.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For all invertible measure-preserving transformations, positive-measure A and distinct zero-constant integer polynomials, find common m,n. No commutation is stated. Standard commuting polynomial recurrence cannot be imported without a bridge.
source_name_literal: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

statement_utf8: Let $a,b$ be distinct positive non-integers. Show that for every ergodic system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$, we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N f(T^{[n^a]}x) \cdot g(T^{[n^b]}x)=\int f \ d\mu \cdot \int g\ d\mu $$ for almost every $x\in X$.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every distinct positive noninteger a,b and ergodic system, bounded f,g: almost-everywhere fractional-power averages equal product integrals. L2 convergence is insufficient for pointwise assertion; no maximal-inequality mechanism proved.
source_name_literal: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

statement_utf8: Suppose that $a,b\in(0,1)$ and $a\neq b$. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T,S)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$ we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(\omega)}f\cdot S^{b_n(\omega)}g= \mathbb E(f|\mathcal{I}_T)\cdot \mathbb E(g|\mathcal{I}_S) $$ where the limit is taken in $L^2(\mu)$ or pointwise.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Almost surely universally over systems and bounded functions, random-time double averages converge in L2 or pointwise to product conditional expectations. Laws of a_n,b_n and independence are missing; L2 and pointwise are distinct endpoints.
source_name_literal: Frantzikinakis - Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2016) (proposed by Nikos Frantzikinakis)

statement_utf8: Starting with an orientation-preserving branched covering $f_0:S^2\to S^2$ and three marked base points, iteratively conjugate it as in Thurston's pullback algorithm to obtain rational maps $r_n$ and coordinate maps $\phi_n$. Under what conditions does $r_n$ converge uniformly to a rational map $r_\infty$, and under what conditions and on what subset of $S^2$ does $\phi_n$ converge uniformly?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Characterize convergence of pullback rational and coordinate maps for arbitrary branched coverings with three basepoints. Markings, normalization and convergence domains required. Critically finite Thurston theory does not characterize the noncritically-finite scope.
source_name_literal: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

statement_utf8: For a Cremer point of an arbitrary rational map, does every neighborhood contain infinitely many periodic orbits?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every neighborhood of every Cremer point of every rational map should contain infinitely many periodic orbits. Density of repelling periodic points in Julia set does not show entire periodic orbits stay in the neighborhood. No small-cycle construction.
source_name_literal: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

statement_utf8: For every real $c\in[-2,1/4]$, is the Julia set of $f_c(z)=z^2+c$ locally connected?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All real quadratic parameters in [-2,1/4], including infinitely renormalizable maps, have locally connected Julia sets. Nonrenormalizable/local special cases do not settle all c. Long renormalization dependency burden; no new elementary route.
source_name_literal: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

statement_utf8: Let $\varphi$ be a holomorphic germ fixing $z_0$ with multiplier $e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ for irrational $\alpha$. Can $\varphi^n(z)\to z_0$ uniformly on some domain?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Existence of a domain of uniform convergence of iterates to irrationally indifferent fixed point. Domain may exclude fixed point and germ iterates require continued definition. Derivative modulus one only obstructs domains containing a neighborhood of the fixed point, not the full question.
source_name_literal: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and Mikhail Lyubich)

statement_utf8: For every degree $d$, prove that expanding (hyperbolic, Axiom A) maps are dense in the spaces $\operatorname{Rat}_d$ of rational maps and $\operatorname{Poly}_d$ of polynomials.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For every degree, hyperbolicity dense in full rational and polynomial parameter spaces. Real-parameter results or individual perturbations cannot cover complex parameter spaces. No full-scope perturbation scheme.
source_name_literal: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by Curt McMullen)

statement_utf8: Given an explicitly specified smooth orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $F$ of the $2$-sphere, is its topological entropy Turing-computable to arbitrary prescribed error, and can it be computed in useful time? Resolve this in particular for Hénon and standard-map families; in the area-preserving cases, ask the analogous question for measure-theoretic entropy.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All explicitly specified smooth sphere diffeomorphisms and requested families: entropy computable to any error and useful time; also metric entropy in area-preserving cases. Representation and useful-time bound absent; Hénon/standard map domains require reconciliation.
source_name_literal: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by John Milnor)

statement_utf8: Can every closed polyhedron be cut along its surface and unfolded into one piece in the plane without overlap? Such an unfolding is called a general unfolding to distinguish from edge-unfoldings (see Problem 9) and vertex-unfoldings (see Problem 42).
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every closed polyhedron admits a connected nonoverlapping general unfolding. Edge or vertex unfolding examples do not answer arbitrary surface cuts. Surface topology and allowed disconnected vertex neighborhoods need primary conventions; no finite universal cut algorithm.
source_name_literal: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

statement_utf8: Given an arbitrary polygon, transform it by a finite sequence of ``vertex-centroid'' moves to a regular polygon. A vertex-centroid move is a translation of a vertex $v$ along the line $vm$, where $m$ is the centroid of the vertices of the polygon, i.e., $1/n$-th of the sum of the vertex coordinates. Vertices may move only one at a time, but in any order and any number of times.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every arbitrary polygon should reach a regular one after finitely many one-vertex translations along its current centroid line. Need simple-polygon and intermediate-degeneracy conventions. Linear rank/invertibility of individual updates alone does not generate all target configurations; inspect primary before a control calculation. Primary TOPP60 entire short entry read: n=3 two-move result is already known; no n>=4 full-scope mechanism established. Bounded successor search returned this primary page; no absence-of-prior inference.
source_name_literal: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

statement_utf8: Is the Yao-Yao Graph a $t$-spanner for constant $t$? A geometric graph is a $t$-spanner (or just a spanner) if, for every pair of nodes, the shortest distance between the nodes following the edges of the graph is at most $t$ times the Euclidean distance between them. See below for the definition of the Yao-Yao graph.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Yao-Yao graph should have a constant stretch bound for all node sets. Cone count, incoming-edge pruning, ties and directed/undirected convention are absent ('See below'). Different cone counts have different behavior; cannot assign a single theorem without source. Primary TOPP70 recovers equally spaced cone definition and incoming shortest-edge pruning, then undirected distances. Li-Zhan ESA2016 Theorem2 proves YY_(2k) is a spanner for each k>=42; final proof combination read. This defeats a new existence-of-suitable-cone-count result; does not answer all integer cone counts. Full dependency audit and odd-cone successor body not read.
source_name_literal: Open Problems Project - Computational Geometry

statement_utf8: What can be said about boundaries arising from strict hyperbolization constructions of Charney and Davis, [18]?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Open-ended classification of boundaries from strict hyperbolization, not a single universal equation. Need Charney-Davis construction and desired invariant. A single computable boundary is not full-scope resolution.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Nadia Benakli)

statement_utf8: Suppose that Z is a compact metrizable topological space, G↷ Z is a convergence action which is topologically transitive, i.e. each G– orbit is dense in Z. Is there a Gromov-hyperbolic space X with the ideal boundary Z so that the action G ↷ Z extends to a uniformly quasi-isometric quasi-action G↷ X?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every minimal convergence action on compact metrizable Z should extend to uniformly quasi-isometric quasi-action on hyperbolic X with boundary Z. 'Topologically transitive' is defined here as every orbit dense (minimal). Known special geometrically finite actions do not supply all actions.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

statement_utf8: Can exotic homology manifolds as in [14] appear as ideal boundaries of Coxeter groups?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Existence of exotic homology manifolds 'as in [14]' as Coxeter ideal boundaries. Reference defines exotic class and geometry needed; arbitrary homology-sphere examples do not meet it. No exact construction proposed.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

statement_utf8: Suppose that ( N1, ∆1) and (N2, ∆2) are closed 3-manifolds equipped with ﬂag-triangulations, so that ∂∞C(N1, ∆1) = ∂∞C(N2, ∆2). Does it follow that every prime connected sum summand of Ni appears as a connected sum summand of Ni+1, i = 1, 2? What can be said in higher dimensions?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Boundary equality of Coxeter constructions from flag triangulated closed3-manifolds should force equality of prime summands, plus higher-dimensional inquiry. C(N,Delta), equality/homeomorphism and index Ni+1 conventions need source; cannot infer rigidity from a guessed construction.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich, Tadeusz Januszkiewicz)

statement_utf8: Let Z be a compactum which is a Z-boundary of a group G. Then Z is never a Boltyansky compactum. In the special case when Z is an Markov compactum, so that all building blocks Kσ → σ are isomorphic, it was proven in [29] that Z cannot be a Boltyansky compactum.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every group Z-boundary compactum should fail Boltyansky dimension drop. Standard check is dim(ZxZ)<2dim(Z); requires finite-dimensional/convention hypotheses. Equal-block Markov case is explicitly already proved, so extending only it earns no credit.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Alexander Dranishnikov)

statement_utf8: Examples of Kleiner and Croke [22], [23] of non-unique boundaries are badly non-locally-connected. Is that essential in having the “ﬂexibility” to have many boundaries? That is, does local connectedness imply uniqueness of the boundary (in the 1-ended case) for CAT(0) groups?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: All one-ended CAT(0) groups: does local connectedness imply boundary uniqueness? Visual-boundary homeomorphism versus equivariant uniqueness must be fixed. Existing badly nonlocally connected examples cannot simply be repurposed.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Kim Ruane)

statement_utf8: Let f: Bn → Bn be a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Can f be approximated by globally quasiconformal diﬀeomorphisms fj: Bn → Bn? Can this be done so that fj’s are K-quasiconformal for all j?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every quasiconformal ball homeomorphism should be approximable by global QC diffeomorphisms, optionally common K. Topology, dimension and K dependence unspecified; smoothing coordinate charts does not preserve a uniform distortion bound automatically.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

statement_utf8: Let G be a hyperbolic group. Is it true that G admit a uniformly quasiconformal discrete action on Sn (for some n)?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every hyperbolic group should admit a discrete uniformly quasiconformal sphere action for some dimension. Embedding boundary into sphere is insufficient to extend the group action with uniform dilatation. No constructive full-group extension.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Misha Kapovich)

statement_utf8: Is there an equivariant continuous map (called Cannon–Thurston map) from the unit circle S1 (the ideal boundary of G as an abstract group) to S2? Then Problem 64 is equivalent to 66.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Circle-to-sphere equivariant Cannon-Thurston map for G from preceding source context; group/representation and Problem64 omitted. General subgroup formulation is separate388799; do not substitute it for this literal target. Kapovich p18 Problem66 is a surface Kleinian representation question; preceding context and Remark27 identify a claimed Mj solution. Baker-Riley general subgroup obstruction cannot be substituted for this narrower representation. Claimed complete Mj body not read.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005)

statement_utf8: Let H ⊂ G be a hyperbolic subgroup of a hyperbolic group (we do not assume that H is quasiconvex). Is it true that there exists an equivariant continuous map ∂∞H → ∂∞G. See [46] for partial results in this direction.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every hyperbolic subgroup of a hyperbolic group, without quasiconvexity, should admit a boundary map. A known-looking nonexistence construction is a prior-art objection requiring actual body confirmation; quasi-convex inclusion handles only a subclass. No new construction invested. Kapovich p18 Problem67 matches general hyperbolic-subgroup question. Baker-Riley author PDF dated August13,2013, Theorem1 gives hyperbolic G and rank3 free H with no Cannon-Thurston map. Read theorem, construction setup and final proof on pp6-7, including escaping H geodesics whose G geodesics pass through identity. Standard identification of equivariant boundary maps with inclusion extension via attracting fixed-point density is not independently audited here. Published theorem is a decisive screening prior objection, not a fresh proof or complete dependency audit.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Mahan Mitra)

statement_utf8: What is the Poisson boundary of the free group with an arbitrary measure?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Identify Poisson boundary for every probability measure on a free group. Degenerate-support, moment and entropy cases differ; geometric boundary identification under finite-moment hypotheses does not cover arbitrary measures.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Vadim Kaimanovich)

statement_utf8: There almost surely exists a horofunction h such that lim n→∞ − 1 n h(xn) = A, where A = lim n→∞ 1 n d(x0, xn). A theorem of Karlsson states that ∀ϵ > 0 there exists a horofunction hϵ such that A − ϵ ≤ − 1 n hϵ(xn) ≤ A + ϵ for all n ≥ N (ϵ).
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Almost-sure single horofunction attaining drift limit, stronger than separate epsilon horofunctions. Space/cocycle, integrability and stationarity hypotheses missing. Compactness of h_epsilon does not justify interchanging time and epsilon limits.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by Conjecture of Anders Karlsson)

statement_utf8: Prove that every arithmetic lattice in Isom( Hn) ( n ≥ 4) is non-coherent. See [38] for some partial results in this direction. It is well-known that every lattice in Isom( HHn) ( n ≥ 2) has Property T.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every arithmetic lattice in real-hyperbolic Isom(H^n), n>=4, should contain a finitely generated non-finitely-presented subgroup. The trailing quaternionic property-T sentence is distinct context; no direct coherence implication. No full arithmetic-family mechanism.
source_name_literal: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005) (proposed by M. Kapovich, L. Potyagailo, E.B. Vinberg)

statement_utf8: An optimist would expect similar inequalities distg(∂−,∂+) <δ =δ(Y ) <∞ (ideally withδ = 2π dim(Y )+1) for metricsg on Y ×[−1,+1]with Sc(g) ≥n(n−1) for all closed manifoldsY of dimensions≠4, which themselvesadmit no metrics withSc > 0.

Brian White told me about 30 years ago that he believed that Volume minimising hypersurfaces in generic Riemannian manifoldsX are non-singular: singularities disappear under arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of metrics inX. This was conﬁrmed in 1993 by Nathan Smale, [118] forn= 8, which extends the Schoen-Yau theorem ton= 8.

statement_utf8: For instance, letX be homomorphic to CP 2 and letvol(Uδ(S)) ≥δ2 for allT(X)-non-spin surfacesS ⊂X and 0<δ ≤1. Is then spin-area(X) ≥1/1 000 000?
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For CP2-type X and every tangent-nonspin surface S, all 0<delta<=1 have tubular volume>=delta²; infer spin-area>=10^-6. spin-area and T(X)-nonspin absent; 'homomorphic' cannot be silently corrected. No test on guessed metric.

statement_utf8: But it is also not impossible that all manifolds admit immersions into the unit ball in the Hilbert spaceR∞with principal curvatures bounded by a universal constant, say by 1 000 000.
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every manifold should immerse in Hilbert unit ball with one universal bound on principal curvatures. Metric prescribed versus induced, manifold dimension and infinite-codimension curvature convention are crucial. Coordinate sine embeddings do not give universal operator curvature automatically.

statement_utf8: Conjecture. Non-Riemannian Guth-Geroch. Let X be an n-dimensional Q-essential pseudomanifold (e.g. manifold) with an arbitrary metric. Then the universal covering˜X of X contains balls of all radiiR the Hilbert volumes of which are≥than these of the EuclideanR-balls, Hilbert-volume( ˜B(R)) ≥vol(Bn Eucl(R)).
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: Every Q-essential n-pseudomanifold with arbitrary metric: for each radius a lifted ball reaches Euclidean Hilbert volume. Exact Hilbert volume and metric regularity are missing; arbitrary rescaling alone is not a counterexample because the small-scale volume normalization also changes.

statement_utf8: For every $\ell,k>0$, there exist $C,L,K>0$ with the following effect. Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with injectivity radius $inj(M,g)\geq \ell$ and Ricci curvature $Ric(g)\geq k$. Then there exists a metric $h$ on $M$ with $inj(M,h)\geq L$ and $|Ric(h)|\leq K$ such that $$ \frac{1}{C}\,g\leq h\leq C\,g. $$
technical_review_quantifiers_and_obstruc: For every ell,k>0 choose uniform C,L,K for all complete manifolds with inj>=ell and Ric>=k, then a bilipschitz bounded-Ricci metric. Dimension dependence and tensor convention need source; smoothing under lower Ricci alone is not automatic. No compactness-based construction established.
